name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
summary: 24/7 professional crisis counseling for child abuse, neglect, and other family issues.

sections.title: About the Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
sections.text: The Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline is a 24-hour hotline dedicated to the prevention of child abuse and serving children and adults who have been victims of abuse or neglect. Operated by Childhelp, one of the nation's leading organizations for child abuse prevention and treatment, the hotline provides crisis intervention, information, and referrals to emergency, social service, and support resources. Professional crisis counselors answer calls around the clock, providing immediate support and guidance.

sections.title: Who Can Call the Hotline
sections.text: Anyone can call—children who are being abused or neglected, adult survivors of childhood abuse, parents who need help or are struggling with parenting challenges, concerned family members, neighbors, or teachers who suspect a child is being abused, and professionals seeking information or resources. The hotline serves people in crisis as well as those seeking information about child abuse prevention, reporting requirements, or local resources.

sections.title: How to Reach the Hotline
sections.text: Call 1-800-4-A-CHILD (1-800-422-4453) any time, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The hotline is staffed by professional crisis counselors who can provide immediate support and connect callers with local resources. Services are available in English and Spanish, with access to interpreters in over 170 languages. All calls are confidential. The hotline does not directly report abuse but can provide guidance on how to make a report in your area if needed.

sections.title: What the Hotline Provides
sections.text: Hotline counselors provide crisis intervention for children and adults in immediate distress, information about child abuse signs, reporting procedures, and prevention, emotional support for survivors of childhood abuse, guidance for parents struggling with parenting challenges, referrals to local child protective services, counseling services, and support groups, and resources for professionals working with children and families. Counselors help callers understand their options and take next steps.

sections.title: About Childhelp
sections.text: Childhelp is a national nonprofit organization dedicated to helping victims of child abuse and neglect. Founded in 1959, Childhelp operates the National Child Abuse Hotline, residential treatment facilities for severely abused children, child advocacy centers, foster care, and adoption programs. The organization's mission is to meet the physical, emotional, educational, and spiritual needs of abused, neglected, and at-risk children. Childhelp also works on prevention through education programs and advocacy for child protection laws.
